settings.heading: When every test comes back normal but you still don't feel right.
How nattokinase works: clearing the body's own "web"

settings.text:
Nattokinase is a serine protease that supports the body's natural fibrinolytic system — the cleanup crew that clears excess fibrin (the same protein that forms scabs and, in larger amounts, contributes to the matrix of arterial plaque and clots).

It works by inactivating PAI-1, the brake your body normally puts on clot dissolution. By releasing that brake, plasmin — your built-in clot-dissolving enzyme — can do its job. Mechanism documented in Tanikawa 2022 and 40+ years of fibrinolysis research.

A common worry: "won't dissolving fibrin loosen plaque and cause a stroke?" The peer-reviewed evidence is reassuring. In Chen 2022's 12-month study of 1,062 adults at 10,800 FU/day — well above what most people take — zero adverse events were recorded. Toxicology (Lampe & English 2016) finds no concern at 1,000–14,000 FU/day.

That said: if you take vitamin-K-antagonist anticoagulants (warfarin), DOACs (Eliquis, Xarelto), or aspirin, talk to your prescribing physician before starting. We removed K2 specifically to make this product compatible with that conversation.

settings.title: Recent research on post-viral microvascular health.
settings.body: Two newer findings widen nattokinase's relevance for people interested in microvascular and post-viral research. Tanikawa et al. (2022, Molecules) showed in vitro that purified nattokinase degrades the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and ACE2 in 60–180 minutes — a cell-lysate / lab-bench study, not yet a human trial. Separately, Grixti, Pretorius & Kell (2024, preprint) showed that recombinant nattokinase degrades fibrinaloid microclots — the anomalous, fibrinolysis-resistant clots documented in Long COVID and ME/CFS — within 2 hours in vitro. Both findings are mechanistic; neither is a human clinical trial yet.

settings.title: What is nattokinase?
settings.content: Nattokinase is a serine-protease enzyme extracted from natto, a traditional Japanese fermented soybean food. Discovered in Tokyo in 1980 by Dr. Hiroyuki Sumi, it's been studied for over 40 years for its activity on fibrin — the protein involved in blood clotting and the matrix of arterial plaque.

settings.title: Why 4,000 FU per capsule? How many should I take?
settings.content:
The largest clinical study to date — Chen et al. (2022, Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine, n=1,062, 12 months) — concludes the clinically active range is 6,000–12,000 FU per day. We picked 4,000 FU per capsule so you can dose to your protocol with your clinician: 1 capsule = 4,000 FU (entry); 2 capsules = ~8,000 FU (within active range); 3 capsules = ~12,000 FU (matches Chen 2022 range).

Why not pre-pack 10,800 FU into a single capsule? Because protocols differ. Some people start low and titrate; some want flexibility around days they take an aspirin or a long flight; some are starting fresh and want maintenance dosing. Per-capsule is per-protocol.

settings.title: Is it safe with Eliquis, Xarelto, warfarin, or aspirin?
settings.content:
Talk to your prescribing physician before starting. Nattokinase has fibrinolytic activity, so the conversation matters. We removed vitamin K2 specifically because K2 interacts with vitamin-K-antagonists like warfarin.

The peer-reviewed evidence: Chen 2022 reported no adverse events across 1,062 adults at 10,800 FU/day for 12 months. Their aspirin co-administration arm (n=96, 100 mg/day) was synergistic for lipids without bleeding events. None of the published trials are randomized safety studies in DOAC users — which is precisely why the conversation belongs with your care team, not us.

settings.title: Why did you remove K2? Can I get it from you?
settings.content:
K2 (menaquinone-7, MK-7) can interact with vitamin-K-antagonist blood thinners like warfarin. Many nattokinase products bundle K2 in by default, which makes them incompatible with that population. We removed it to maximize compatibility — and we're honest about it: Chen 2022 actually shows K2 was synergistic with nattokinase for lipid endpoints (TC –17.6% with K2 vs –16.3% without).

If you don't take vitamin-K-antagonists and want the K2 + NK synergy Chen 2022 describes, we sell K2 MK-7 separately — $14 standalone, $9 when bundled with Spike Detox.

settings.title: How long until I notice a difference?
settings.content: Honest answer: it varies, and no one can promise an outcome. Chen 2022 measured cardiovascular endpoints at 12 months. The microclot in vitro work (Grixti/Kell 2024 preprint) acts within hours in a test tube but in-vivo translation isn't established. We don't make week-by-week promises about how you'll feel.

settings.title: When should I take it?
settings.content: On an empty stomach, ideally 30 minutes before a meal or before bed. Food can reduce enzyme activity. Many people split into morning + evening doses if taking 2–3 capsules.

settings.title: What happens if I stop taking it?
settings.content: Many people use Spike Detox as ongoing cardiovascular support, similar to how they'd use a daily vitamin. Others use it for time-limited protocols around specific events (recovery, travel, post-illness). Talk to your healthcare provider about what makes sense for your situation. There's no withdrawal effect documented in the published literature — but ongoing structure-function support is a different question, and only your clinician can advise on your specific case.
